key_insight: Probability-based rewards in verifier-free RL can collapse on long reasoning traces, making different answers look nearly identical and destabilizing optimization.
engineering_relevance: For LLM training pipelines, RLCPR offers a practical way to improve reward reliability, token efficiency, and training stability when no external verifier is available.
method: Uncertainty-aware data sampling filters out rollouts likely to suffer posterior concentration before generation.
Concentration-aware regularization discourages unnecessarily long traces when posterior rewards have already collapsed.
The framework is designed to work in GRPO-style verifier-free reinforcement learning settings.
evidence_signal: Across six of seven benchmarks spanning general-domain and mathematical reasoning, RLCPR improves over the strongest verifier-free RL baseline by up to 4.0% while using fewer tokens.
watch_item: The method depends on detecting posterior concentration reliably; if this signal is noisy or poorly calibrated, the regularization and sampling decisions may be less effective.
paper_title: Rethinking Probability-Based Reinforcement Learning From Posterior Concentration
